0112| ## Interactive session
0113| 
0114| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0115| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0116| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0117| command.
0118| 
0119| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0120| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0121| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0122| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0123| again.
0124| 
0125| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0126| 
0127| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0128| | --- | --- |
0129| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0130| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0131| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0132| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0133| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0134| | `pause` | pausing work |
0135| | `resume` | resuming work |
0136| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0137| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0138| 
0139| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0140| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0141| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0142| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0143| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0144| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0145| 
0146| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0147| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0148| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0149| 
0150| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0151| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0152| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0153| 
0154| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0155| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0156| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0157| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.

0159| ## Commands
0160| 
0161| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0162| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0163| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0164| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0165| 
0166| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0167| | --- | --- | --- |
0168| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0169| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0170| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0171| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0172| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0173| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0174| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0175| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0176| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0177| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0178| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0179| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0180| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |

0182| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0183| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0184| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0185| exits with a non-zero code.

0188| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0189| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0190| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:

0194| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0195| ```

0197| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0198| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0199| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0200| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0201| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0202| locale.

0204| ### Output
0205| 
0206| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0207| exactly one JSON object to stdout:

0211| ```

0224| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine

#!/bin/sh
# Forgel Code installer.
#
# One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
#
# The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
# ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
# directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
# interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
# from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
# shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
# $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
# block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
# cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
# A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
# the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
# whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
# absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
# never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
# started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
# are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
# ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
# the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
#
# Environment variables:
#   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
#   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
#   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
#   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)
#   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
#   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
#   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
#   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
#   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
#   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
#
# The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.

set -eu

# The exact markers an uninstall looks for. They are compared byte for byte.
MARKER_START='# >>> forgel-code >>>'
MARKER_END='# <<< forgel-code <<<'

# A profile whose last line has no final newline cannot be restored byte for
# byte from the block alone: the newline that separates that line from the
# block is indistinguishable from one the file always had. The installer
# records the case in one comment line directly above the block and removes
# that line, with the separator newline, together with the block.
MARKER_SEPARATOR='# forgel-code: the line above had no final newline'

HOME_DIR=${HOME:-/}
PREFIX=${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME_DIR/.local/share/forgel-code}
BIN_DIR=${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME_DIR/.local/bin}
LAUNCHER=$BIN_DIR/forgel-code
TAG=${FORGEL_CODE_TAG:-v0.2.0}
REPOSITORY=${FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY:-https://github.com/forgel-dev/code}

# What a fresh shell reports back: its own PATH and the path it resolves
# ``forgel-code`` to. The prefixes keep the answer readable next to anything a
# system-wide profile may print.
CHECK_PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
CHECK_COMMAND='printf "forgel-fresh-path=%s\n" "$PATH"; fresh=$(command -v forgel-code || true); printf "forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\n" "$fresh"'

# The bound for the fresh-shell check, in seconds, when FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT is
# unset, and the grace period the checked shell gets between the graceful stop
# and the forceful one. A login shell reads its startup files in milliseconds;
# ten seconds leaves room on a slow machine and still bounds a shell that never
# answers.
DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMIT=10
VERIFY_GRACE=2

# How long the installer waits for the watchdog's decision, in whole seconds,
# derived from the grace period. One polling step of the watchdog is the longest
# the decision can take after the checked command exits, so one grace period
# covers it with room to spare. A watchdog that never answers cannot hold the
# installer longer than this.
DECISION_WAIT=$VERIFY_GRACE
if [ "$DECISION_WAIT" -lt 1 ]; then
    DECISION_WAIT=1
fi

# The profile files this installer can have written. ``--uninstall`` cleans the
# block out of every one of them, so no stale PATH entry stays behind. The list
# is a superset of what the install path may edit, including ~/.bashrc, because
# a non-login bash session reads that file and an earlier installation could
# have left its block there.
PROFILE_NAMES='.zshrc .zprofile .zshenv .bash_profile .bash_login .profile .bashrc'

# Set by ``verify_profile`` once the fresh shell resolved the launcher.
VERIFIED_PATH=

# What the bounded check owns while it runs: its private directory, the command
# it started, the process group that command leads and the watchdog that bounds
# it. Every one of them is released by ``cleanup_check``, whichever way the
# script ends.
CHECK_DIR=
CHECK_CHILD=
CHECK_GROUP=
CHECK_WATCHER=

# Set by ``cleanup_check`` once the current check has been released, so the exit
# trap and a signal trap cannot release the same check twice.
CHECK_CLEANED=

# Set by ``bounded_run``: the exit status of the checked command and what it
# printed. A status of 124 means the bound elapsed.
CHECK_STATUS=0
CHECK_OUTPUT=

usage() {
    cat <<'USAGE'
Usage: install.sh [--uninstall] [--help]

Installs the Forgel Code client into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}
and its launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, adding that directory
to PATH with one marked block in the profile the login shell reads. The result
is checked in a freshly started login interactive shell under a bounded time
limit.

  --uninstall   remove the installation, the launcher and the PATH block
  --help        show this text

Set FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 to leave the shell profile untouched; the
script then prints the exact export PATH=... line to add yourself.
USAGE
}

detect_python() {
    if [ -n "${FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON"
        return 0
    fi
    if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        command -v python3
        return 0
    fi
    if command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        command -v python
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# A directory counts as a checkout only when it is this project, so a stray
# pyproject.toml next to the caller cannot silently install another package.
is_forgel_code_source() {
    directory=$1
    if [ -z "$directory" ] || [ ! -d "$directory" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    if [ ! -d "$directory/forgel_code" ] || [ ! -f "$directory/pyproject.toml" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    grep -q 'name = "forgel-code"' "$directory/pyproject.toml"
}

# The directory holding this script. With ``curl ... | sh`` there is none.
script_directory() {
    case ${0:-} in
        */*) cd -P -- "${0%/*}" 2>/dev/null && pwd ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

resolve_source() {
    if [ -n "${FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE:-}" ]; then
        if ! is_forgel_code_source "$FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE"; then
            echo "install.sh: FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE is not a Forgel Code checkout: $FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "$FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE"
        return 0
    fi
    for candidate in "$(script_directory 2>/dev/null || true)" "$(pwd)"; do
        if is_forgel_code_source "$candidate"; then
            printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$REPOSITORY/archive/refs/tags/$TAG.tar.gz"
}

# The account login shell: the macOS Directory Service entry first, then the
# passwd database. Prints nothing when neither source answers.
account_login_shell() {
    if command -v dscl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        found=$(dscl . -read "$HOME_DIR" UserShell 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^UserShell:[[:space:]]*//p' | head -n 1) || found=
        if [ -n "$found" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$found"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    user=$(id -u 2>/dev/null) || user=
    if [ -n "$user" ]; then
        found=
        if command -v getent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            found=$(getent passwd "$user" 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f7 | head -n 1) || found=
        fi
        if [ -z "$found" ] && [ -r /etc/passwd ]; then
            found=$(awk -F: -v u="$user" '$3 == u { print $7; exit }' /etc/passwd) || found=
        fi
        if [ -n "$found" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$found"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    printf '\n'
}

shell_name() {
    printf '%s\n' "${1##*/}"
}

# The shells whose login sessions this installer can place a PATH block for.
is_handled_shell() {
    case $(shell_name "$1") in
        zsh|bash|sh|dash|ksh|ksh93|mksh|pdksh|ash|yash) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# The shell of the invoking process, read with ps. A piped run often has no
# useful $SHELL but a meaningful parent shell. Prints nothing when that process
# is not a shell this installer handles or cannot be resolved.
parent_login_shell() {
    if ! command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 1
    fi
    pid=${PPID:-}
    if [ -z "$pid" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    found=$(ps -p "$pid" -o comm= 2>/dev/null) || found=
    found=${found%%[[:space:]]*}
    # A login shell often reports itself as ``-zsh``.
    found=${found#-}
    if [ -z "$found" ] || ! is_handled_shell "$found"; then
        return 1
    fi
    if ! resolved=$(command -v "$found" 2>/dev/null) || [ -z "$resolved" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$resolved"
}

# The shell that reads the edited profile for an interactive login session.
# $SHELL decides when it names a shell we handle; otherwise the invoking process
# and then the account login shell decide, and a POSIX ``sh`` is the last
# resort, which reads $HOME/.profile. An empty $SHELL never decides for bash by
# itself.
detect_login_shell() {
    candidate=${SHELL:-}
    if [ -n "$candidate" ] && is_handled_shell "$candidate"; then
        printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
        return 0
    fi
    candidate=$(parent_login_shell) || candidate=
    if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
        return 0
    fi
    candidate=$(account_login_shell) || candidate=
    if [ -n "$candidate" ] && is_handled_shell "$candidate"; then
        printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s\n' /bin/sh
}

shell_family() {
    case $(shell_name "$1") in
        zsh) printf '%s\n' zsh ;;
        bash) printf '%s\n' bash ;;
        *) printf '%s\n' posix ;;
    esac
}

# Which profile file an interactive login session of the detected shell reads.
# The block never goes into $HOME/.bashrc alone: a login bash does not read it.
profile_path() {
    if [ -n "${FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE"
        return 0
    fi
    case $(shell_family "$DETECTED_SHELL") in
        zsh)
            printf '%s\n' "$HOME_DIR/.zshrc"
            ;;
        bash)
            for name in .bash_profile .bash_login .profile; do
                if [ -f "$HOME_DIR/$name" ]; then
                    printf '%s\n' "$HOME_DIR/$name"
                    return 0
                fi
            done
            printf '%s\n' "$HOME_DIR/.bash_profile"
            ;;
        *)
            printf '%s\n' "$HOME_DIR/.profile"
            ;;
    esac
}

no_profile_edit() {
    case ${FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH:-} in
        ''|0|false|no|off) ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac
    case ${FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT:-} in
        ''|0|false|no|off) ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# The marked block. Its body is a POSIX ``case ":$PATH:"`` guard: the launcher
# directory is prepended only when it is not already in PATH, so sourcing the
# block twice, or from several profiles, leaves one entry in PATH.
print_block() {
    printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_START"
    printf 'case ":$PATH:" in\n'
    printf '    *":%s:"*) ;;\n' "$BIN_DIR"
    printf '    *) PATH="%s:$PATH" ;;\n' "$BIN_DIR"
    printf 'esac\n'
    printf 'export PATH\n'
    printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_END"
}

# Whether the last byte of the file is a newline.
ends_with_newline() {
    [ -s "$1" ] || return 1
    [ "$(tail -c 1 "$1" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "1" ]
}

# Whether a start marker is left open, without an end marker after it. Such a
# block is not a block: where it ends is unknown, so it is never removed and the
# file is left exactly as it is. Status 0 means an open marker was found, 1 a
# well-formed or marker-free file, anything else that the file is unreadable.
has_unclosed_block() {
    awk -v start="$MARKER_START" -v end="$MARKER_END" '
        $0 == start { inside = 1; next }
        $0 == end { inside = 0 }
        END { exit (inside ? 0 : 1) }
    ' "$1"
}

# Drop the marked block, if there is one. Every other line is kept byte for
# byte, including whether the file ended with a newline: the rewrite carries
# the last line without a terminator when the input had none. A block this
# installer appended after a last line that had no final newline carries the
# separator comment, and both go away, so uninstall restores the original. An
# unterminated start marker is reported and the file is left untouched, because
# removing everything from that marker on would delete unrelated content.
remove_profile_block() {
    profile=$1
    if [ ! -f "$profile" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ! grep -Fq "$MARKER_START" "$profile"; then
        return 0
    fi
    scan=0
    has_unclosed_block "$profile" || scan=$?
    case $scan in
        0)
            echo "install.sh: $profile has a '$MARKER_START' line with no matching '$MARKER_END' line; leaving the file unchanged. Repair that block and run install.sh again." >&2
            return 1
            ;;
        1) ;;
        *)
            echo "install.sh: cannot read $profile" >&2
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    tmp=$profile.forgel-code.$$
    if ! cp -p "$profile" "$tmp"; then
        echo "install.sh: cannot write next to $profile" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    final_newline=0
    if ends_with_newline "$profile"; then
        final_newline=1
    fi
    if ! awk -v start="$MARKER_START" -v end="$MARKER_END" \
            -v separator="$MARKER_SEPARATOR" -v final_newline="$final_newline" '
            { text[NR] = $0 }
            END {
                total = NR
                kept = 0
                inside = 0
                block_end = 0
                for (i = 1; i <= total; i++) {
                    if (inside == 0 && text[i] == start) {
                        inside = 1
                        block_end = 0
                        continue
                    }
                    if (inside == 1) {
                        if (text[i] == end) {
                            inside = 0
                            block_end = i
                        }
                        continue
                    }
                    kept++
                    kept_text[kept] = text[i]
                    kept_index[kept] = i
                }
                restore_missing_newline = 0
                if (block_end == total && kept > 0 && kept_text[kept] == separator) {
                    kept--
                    restore_missing_newline = 1
                }
                for (i = 1; i <= kept; i++) {
                    terminate = 1
                    if (i == kept && restore_missing_newline == 1) {
                        terminate = 0
                    } else if (i == kept && kept_index[i] == total && final_newline == 0) {
                        terminate = 0
                    }
                    if (terminate) {
                        printf "%s\n", kept_text[i]
                    } else {
                        printf "%s", kept_text[i]
                    }
                }
            }
        ' "$profile" > "$tmp"; then
        rm -f "$tmp"
        echo "install.sh: cannot rewrite $profile" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! mv "$tmp" "$profile"; then
        rm -f "$tmp"
        echo "install.sh: cannot replace $profile" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Exactly one block, whatever the profile already held. The previous block is
# removed first and only then is the new one appended, so an interrupted run
# leaves one block at most. The append is byte-stable: a second run over the
# same profile rewrites it to the same bytes, and a last line without a final
# newline is recorded so the block can be dropped without leaving a newline
# behind.
add_profile_block() {
    profile=$1
    case $profile in
        */*) mkdir -p "${profile%/*}" || return 1 ;;
    esac
    if ! remove_profile_block "$profile"; then
        return 1
    fi
    {
        if [ -s "$profile" ] && ! ends_with_newline "$profile"; then
            printf '\n'
            printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_SEPARATOR"
        fi
        print_block
    } >> "$profile" || return 1
    return 0
}

# The bound in seconds: FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT when it is a positive integer, the
# built-in default otherwise.
verify_limit() {
    configured=${FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT:-}
    case $configured in
        ''|*[!0-9]*)
            printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMIT"
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
    if [ "$configured" -lt 1 ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMIT"
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$configured"
}

# The current time in milliseconds, so the check can be timed. A ``date`` with
# nanoseconds answers with them; one without that extension (macOS writes the
# literal ``N``) falls back to the interpreter the installer already requires,
# and to whole seconds only when nothing finer answers. A host with no usable
# clock reports 0, and the verdict is then the recorded timeout alone.
now_millis() {
    stamp=$(date +%s%N 2>/dev/null) || stamp=
    case $stamp in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp= ;;
    esac
    if [ "${#stamp}" -ge 19 ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$((stamp / 1000000))"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -n "${PYTHON:-}" ]; then
        stamp=$("$PYTHON" -c 'import time; print(int(time.time() * 1000))' 2>/dev/null) || stamp=
        case $stamp in
            ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp= ;;
        esac
        if [ -n "$stamp" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$stamp"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    stamp=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || stamp=
    case $stamp in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) stamp=0 ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\n' "$((stamp * 1000))"
}

# An unpredictable name component, so the check directory cannot be guessed
# and pre-created by another user.
random_token() {
    token=
    if [ -r /dev/urandom ] && command -v od >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        token=$(od -An -N 8 -tx1 /dev/urandom 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n') || token=
    fi
    case $token in
        ''|*[!0-9a-f]*) token= ;;
    esac
    if [ -z "$token" ]; then
        token=$$$$$$
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$token"
}

# A directory only the current user can enter or read, under the system
# temporary directory, with a name nobody can predict.
create_check_dir() {
    parent=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}
    if [ -z "$parent" ] || [ ! -d "$parent" ]; then
        parent=/tmp
    fi
    attempt=0
    while [ "$attempt" -lt 10 ]; do
        candidate=$parent/forgel-code-check.$(random_token)
        if (umask 077 && mkdir -m 700 "$candidate" 2>/dev/null); then
            CHECK_DIR=$candidate
            return 0
        fi
        attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    done
    echo "install.sh: cannot create a private directory under $parent" >&2
    return 1
}

# The members of a process group, one pid per line.
process_group() {
    ps -A -o pid= -o pgid= 2>/dev/null | awk -v group="$1" '$2 == group { print $1 }'
}

# Every descendant of a process, one pid per line.
process_tree() {
    ps -A -o pid= -o ppid= 2>/dev/null | awk -v root="$1" '
        { parent[$1] = $2; ids[NR] = $1 }
        END {
            frontier[0] = root
            count = 1
            for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                for (j = 1; j <= NR; j++) {
                    pid = ids[j]
                    if (parent[pid] == frontier[i] && !(pid in seen)) {
                        seen[pid] = 1
                        frontier[count] = pid
                        count++
                    }
                }
            }
            for (i = 1; i < count; i++) print frontier[i]
        }'
}

# Start the checked command in a process group of its own, and record that group
# for the whole lifetime of the check: the command may exit at once while
# something it started lives on in the same group. The launcher puts itself in a
# new session, and so in a new process group, before it runs the command; the
# group id is therefore its own pid. Python is already required to install the
# client. A shell without it falls back to its own job control, and otherwise to
# the descendant sweep alone.
start_check() {
    out=$1
    shift
    if [ -n "${PYTHON:-}" ] && "$PYTHON" -c 'import os' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        "$PYTHON" -c '
import os, sys
try:
    os.setsid()
except OSError:
    try:
        os.setpgid(0, 0)
    except OSError:
        pass
try:
    os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])
except OSError:
    os._exit(127)
' "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
    else
        set -m 2>/dev/null || true
        "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
    fi
    CHECK_CHILD=$!
    set +m 2>/dev/null || true
    CHECK_GROUP=$CHECK_CHILD
    return 0
}

# Signal every member of a process group. The caller's own group is never
# signalled, so a check that could not be placed in a group of its own cannot
# make the cleanup reach the installer itself.
signal_group() {
    signal=$1
    group=$2
    case $group in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    own=
    if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        own=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ') || own=
    fi
    if [ -n "$own" ] && [ "$group" = "$own" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if kill -"$signal" "-$group" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    # A shell that cannot name a group signals its members one by one.
    for pid in $(process_group "$group"); do
        kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    return 0
}

# Stop what the checked command started. The dedicated process group is the
# primary target: everything that stayed in it goes at once, on the success path
# as well as on the timeout path. A sweep of the checked command's descendants
# follows, so a descendant that left the group is reached as well.
stop_check() {
    signal=$1
    signal_group "$signal" "$CHECK_GROUP"
    if [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
        for pid in $(process_tree "$CHECK_CHILD"); do
            kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        done
        kill -"$signal" "$CHECK_CHILD" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    return 0
}

# Release everything the bounded check owns: the watchdog, the checked process
# group with the descendants that left it, and the private directory. It runs at
# most once per check, so the exit trap and a signal trap cannot release the
# same check twice and a second call is a no-op. Every piece of state the
# release reads is cleared only after it has been used.
cleanup_check() {
    if [ -n "$CHECK_CLEANED" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    CHECK_CLEANED=1
    if [ -n "$CHECK_WATCHER" ]; then
        kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
        CHECK_WATCHER=
    fi
    if [ -n "$CHECK_GROUP" ] || [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
        stop_check KILL
        if [ -n "$CHECK_CHILD" ]; then
            wait "$CHECK_CHILD" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        CHECK_GROUP=
        CHECK_CHILD=
    fi
    if [ -n "$CHECK_DIR" ]; then
        rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
        CHECK_DIR=
    fi
    return 0
}

check_interrupted() {
    cleanup_check
    exit "$1"
}

# Wait, for a bounded moment, until the watchdog has recorded its decision in
# the private check directory: ``timed-out`` when the bound had elapsed before
# the checked command exited, ``finished`` when it saw the command gone first.
# Status 0 means the decision is there, 1 that the watchdog did not answer
# within DECISION_WAIT seconds. The decision says which stop to expect; it is
# not the verdict, which is the time the check took (see ``bounded_run``). The
# wait never depends on the checked command, so a watchdog that never answers
# delays the installer by that fixed limit at most.
await_decision() {
    decision_dir=$1
    waited=0
    while :; do
        if [ -e "$decision_dir/timed-out" ] || [ -e "$decision_dir/finished" ]; then
            return 0
        fi
        if [ "$waited" -ge "$DECISION_WAIT" ]; then
            return 1
        fi
        sleep 1 2>/dev/null || true
        waited=$((waited + 1))
    done
}

# Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
# required and is not used: the command runs in the background and a watchdog
# stops it once the bound elapsed. The watchdog records ``timed-out`` in the
# private directory before it starts the graceful stop, and ``finished`` when it
# saw the command gone before the bound; that record says which stop to expect,
# never what the verdict is. The installer times the check itself and reports a
# timeout whenever the measured time reached the bound, so the ordering between
# the command's own exit, the record and the read of the result cannot turn a
# step that overran into a success. A command that finished inside the bound
# keeps its own status, a nonzero one included. After the graceful stop the
# watchdog forcefully stops the rest of the checked command's process group once
# the grace period has passed. Nothing the function starts survives it.
# CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.
#
# The checked command leads a process group of its own (see ``start_check``), so
# the group is what the cleanup signals, on the success path as much as on the
# timeout path. Its three standard descriptors are redirected, so the group has
# no terminal to hold it and cannot stop on a terminal access.
bounded_run() {
    limit=$1
    shift
    CHECK_STATUS=0
    CHECK_OUTPUT=
    CHECK_CLEANED=
    CHECK_CHILD=
    CHECK_GROUP=
    if ! create_check_dir; then
        return 1
    fi
    out=$CHECK_DIR/output
    timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
    finished=$CHECK_DIR/finished
    saved_umask=$(umask)
    umask 077
    if ! : > "$out"; then
        umask "$saved_umask"
        cleanup_check
        return 1
    fi
    started=$(now_millis)
    start_check "$out" "$@"
    umask "$saved_umask"
    child=$CHECK_CHILD
    (
        exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
        sleeper=
        trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
        elapsed=0
        while [ "$elapsed" -lt "$limit" ]; do
            sleep 1 &
            sleeper=$!
            wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
            sleeper=
            elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
            if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
                # The command was gone inside the bound; record that so the
                # caller knows which stop to expect.
                : > "$finished" 2>/dev/null || true
                exit 0
            fi
        done
        : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
        stop_check TERM
        sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
        stop_check KILL
    ) &
    CHECK_WATCHER=$!
    wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
    ended=$(now_millis)
    measured=$((ended - started))
    if await_decision "$CHECK_DIR"; then
        # The watchdog records its decision before it stops anything, so on
        # the timeout path it may still own the graceful then the forceful
        # stop; let it finish so nothing outlives the check.
        wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        # A watchdog that never answers is not allowed to hold the installer. A
        # decision that never arrives is not evidence that the bound was kept;
        # the measured time decides that below.
        kill -KILL "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    # The verdict is the time the check took, never the presence of a record: a
    # step that outlived the bound is a timeout even when it exited on its own
    # before the timeout was recorded, and a step inside the bound keeps its own
    # status, a nonzero one included.
    if [ -e "$timed_out" ] || [ "$measured" -ge "$((limit * 1000))" ]; then
        CHECK_STATUS=124
    fi
    CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
    # The check is released here, before any state the release reads is
    # cleared: a successful check leaves nothing behind, exactly like a failed
    # or a timed-out one.
    cleanup_check
    return 0
}

report_path() {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/^forgel-fresh-path=//p' | tail -n 1
}

report_resolved() {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/^forgel-fresh-resolved=//p' | tail -n 1
}

# The defined failure report: the edited file, the exact block, the shell that
# was checked and the PATH that shell reported.
verification_failure() {
    shell=$1
    profile=$2
    fresh_path=$3
    resolved=$4
    status=$5
    limit=$6
    echo "install.sh: the fresh login shell did not put forgel-code on PATH" >&2
    case $status in
        0) ;;
        124) echo "install.sh: the check was stopped after ${limit}s; a timed-out or signalled check is a failure" >&2 ;;
        start) echo "install.sh: the fresh login shell could not be started" >&2 ;;
        *) echo "install.sh: the fresh login shell exited with status $status" >&2 ;;
    esac
    echo "install.sh: login shell: $shell" >&2
    echo "install.sh: profile file: $profile" >&2
    echo "install.sh: launcher: $LAUNCHER" >&2
    echo "install.sh: PATH block written:" >&2
    print_block >&2
    echo "install.sh: PATH in the fresh shell: ${fresh_path:-<empty>}" >&2
    echo "install.sh: forgel-code resolves to: ${resolved:-<not found>}" >&2
    echo "install.sh: check that $shell reads $profile when it starts a login session" >&2
    return 0
}

# Verify the block in a freshly started login interactive shell. The check
# passes only when that shell answered in time, exited cleanly and resolved
# ``forgel-code`` to the launcher just written, character for character.
verify_profile() {
    shell=$1
    profile=$2
    limit=$(verify_limit)
    report=
    resolved=
    fresh_path=
    status=start
    if [ -n "$shell" ] && [ -x "$shell" ]; then
        if bounded_run "$limit" env -i HOME="$HOME_DIR" SHELL="$shell" TERM=dumb PATH="$CHECK_PATH" "$shell" -l -i -c "$CHECK_COMMAND"; then
            status=$CHECK_STATUS
            report=$CHECK_OUTPUT
            fresh_path=$(report_path "$report")
            resolved=$(report_resolved "$report")
        fi
    fi
    if [ "$status" = "0" ] && [ -n "$resolved" ] && [ "$resolved" = "$LAUNCHER" ]; then
        VERIFIED_PATH=$resolved
        return 0
    fi
    verification_failure "$shell" "$profile" "$fresh_path" "$resolved" "$status" "$limit"
    return 1
}

write_launcher() {
    mkdir -p "$BIN_DIR"
    {
        printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh'
        printf '%s\n' '# Forgel Code launcher written by install.sh; do not edit.'
        printf 'PYTHONPATH="%s${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"\n' "$PREFIX"
        printf '%s\n' 'export PYTHONPATH'
        printf 'exec "%s" -m forgel_code "$@"\n' "$PYTHON"
    } > "$LAUNCHER"
    chmod 755 "$LAUNCHER"
}

add_path() {
    if no_profile_edit; then
        echo "Leaving the shell profile untouched."
        echo "Add this line to your shell profile:"
        printf 'export PATH="%s:$PATH"\n' "$BIN_DIR"
        return 0
    fi
    DETECTED_SHELL=$(detect_login_shell)
    profile=$(profile_path)
    if ! add_profile_block "$profile"; then
        return 1
    fi
    case $(shell_family "$DETECTED_SHELL") in
        posix)
            echo "install.sh: warning: $DETECTED_SHELL is neither zsh nor bash; the PATH block is in $profile" >&2
            ;;
    esac
    if ! verify_profile "$DETECTED_SHELL" "$profile"; then
        return 1
    fi
    echo "Login shell: $DETECTED_SHELL"
    echo "PATH block written to $profile"
    echo "Fresh login shell check: command -v forgel-code -> $VERIFIED_PATH"
    echo "Open a new terminal to pick the change up."
    return 0
}

install_client() {
    if ! PYTHON=$(detect_python); then
        echo "install.sh: no Python 3 interpreter found on PATH" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! "$PYTHON" -c 'import sys; sys.exit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 9) else 1)' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "install.sh: $PYTHON is older than Python 3.9 or cannot run" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! "$PYTHON" -c 'import pip' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "install.sh: $PYTHON has no pip module; install pip and try again" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! SOURCE=$(resolve_source); then
        return 1
    fi
    echo "Installing Forgel Code from $SOURCE"
    mkdir -p "$PREFIX"
    if ! "$PYTHON" -m pip install --target "$PREFIX" --upgrade --no-deps --no-index --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation --no-compile --disable-pip-version-check --no-warn-script-location "$SOURCE"; then
        echo "install.sh: installing the client failed" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! write_launcher; then
        echo "install.sh: cannot write $LAUNCHER" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! installed=$("$LAUNCHER" --version); then
        echo "install.sh: the installed launcher does not run" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$installed"
    echo "Installed into $PREFIX"
    echo "Launcher: $LAUNCHER"
    add_path
}

# Clean the marked block out of one profile file, reporting it only when the
# file really carried one.
uninstall_profile() {
    profile=$1
    if [ ! -f "$profile" ] || ! grep -Fq "$MARKER_START" "$profile"; then
        return 0
    fi
    if remove_profile_block "$profile"; then
        echo "Removed the PATH block from $profile"
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

uninstall() {
    status=0
    if [ -d "$PREFIX" ]; then
        if rm -rf "$PREFIX"; then
            echo "Removed $PREFIX"
        else
            echo "install.sh: cannot remove $PREFIX" >&2
            status=1
        fi
    fi
    if [ -f "$LAUNCHER" ]; then
        if rm -f "$LAUNCHER"; then
            echo "Removed $LAUNCHER"
        else
            echo "install.sh: cannot remove $LAUNCHER" >&2
            status=1
        fi
    fi
    for name in $PROFILE_NAMES; do
        if ! uninstall_profile "$HOME_DIR/$name"; then
            status=1
        fi
    done
    # An install may have written the block into the profile named by
    # FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE instead of one of the standard names, and a run that
    # failed its fresh-shell check leaves the block behind. Clean that path too;
    # it is a no-op when it names a file the loop above already cleaned.
    if [ -n "${FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE:-}" ]; then
        if ! uninstall_profile "$FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE"; then
            status=1
        fi
    fi
    if [ "$status" = "0" ]; then
        echo "Forgel Code is uninstalled."
    fi
    return "$status"
}

main() {
    case ${1:-} in
        '')
            install_client
            ;;
        --uninstall)
            uninstall
            ;;
        -h|--help)
            usage
            ;;
        *)
            echo "install.sh: unknown argument: $1" >&2
            usage >&2
            return 2
            ;;
    esac
}

# Nothing this script started may outlive it, however it ends.
trap 'cleanup_check' EXIT
trap 'check_interrupted 129' HUP
trap 'check_interrupted 130' INT
trap 'check_interrupted 143' TERM

main "$@"

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Interactive session
0113| 
0114| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0115| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0116| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0117| command.
0118| 
0119| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0120| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0121| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0122| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0123| again.
0124| 
0125| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0126| 
0127| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0128| | --- | --- |
0129| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0130| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0131| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0132| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0133| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0134| | `pause` | pausing work |
0135| | `resume` | resuming work |
0136| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0137| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0138| 
0139| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0140| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0141| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0142| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0143| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0144| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0145| 
0146| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0147| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0148| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0149| 
0150| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0151| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0152| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0153| 
0154| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0155| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0156| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0157| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.
0158| 
0159| ## Commands
0160| 
0161| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0162| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0163| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0164| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0165| 
0166| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0167| | --- | --- | --- |
0168| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0169| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0170| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0171| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0172| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0173| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0174| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0175| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0176| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0177| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0178| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0179| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0180| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0181| 
0182| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0183| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0184| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0185| exits with a non-zero code.
0186| 
0187| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0188| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0189| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0190| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0191| 
0192| ```sh
0193| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0194| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0195| ```
0196| 
0197| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0198| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0199| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0200| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0201| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0202| locale.
0203| 
0204| ### Output
0205| 
0206| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0207| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0208| 
0209| ```json
0210| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0211| ```
0212| 
0213| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0214| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0215| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0216| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0217| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0218| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0219| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0220| `forgel` leads the message.
0221| 
0222| ### Active project
0223| 
0224| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0225| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0226| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0227| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0228| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0229| 
0230| ### Timeout
0231| 
0232| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0233| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0234| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0235| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0236| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0237| 
0238| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0239| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0240| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0241| begins with a hyphen.
0242| 
0243| ## Tests
0244| 
0245| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0246| network access:
0247| 
0248| ```sh
0249| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0250| ```
0251| 
0252| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0253| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0254| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0255| directory and a real detected login shell.
0256| 
0257| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0258| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0259| 
0260| ```sh
0261| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]"
0262| python -m pytest -q
0263| ```

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Interactive session
0113| 
0114| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0115| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0116| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0117| command.
0118| 
0119| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0120| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0121| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0122| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0123| again.
0124| 
0125| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0126| 
0127| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0128| | --- | --- |
0129| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0130| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0131| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0132| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0133| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0134| | `pause` | pausing work |
0135| | `resume` | resuming work |
0136| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0137| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0138| 
0139| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0140| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0141| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0142| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0143| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0144| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0145| 
0146| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0147| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0148| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0149| 
0150| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0151| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0152| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0153| 
0154| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0155| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0156| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0157| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.
0158| 
0159| ## Commands
0160| 
0161| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0162| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0163| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0164| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0165| 
0166| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0167| | --- | --- | --- |
0168| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0169| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0170| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0171| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0172| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0173| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0174| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0175| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0176| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0177| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0178| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0179| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0180| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0181| 
0182| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0183| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0184| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0185| exits with a non-zero code.
0186| 
0187| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0188| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0189| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0190| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0191| 
0192| ```sh
0193| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0194| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0195| ```
0196| 
0197| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0198| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0199| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0200| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0201| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0202| locale.
0203| 
0204| ### Output
0205| 
0206| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0207| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0208| 
0209| ```json
0210| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0211| ```
0212| 
0213| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0214| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0215| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0216| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0217| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0218| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0219| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0220| `forgel` leads the message.
0221| 
0222| ### Active project
0223| 
0224| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0225| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0226| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0227| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0228| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0229| 
0230| ### Timeout
0231| 
0232| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0233| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0234| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0235| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0236| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0237| 
0238| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0239| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0240| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0241| begins with a hyphen.
0242| 
0243| ## Tests
0244| 
0245| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0246| network access:
0247| 
0248| ```sh
0249| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0250| ```
0251| 
0252| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0253| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0254| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0255| directory and a real detected login shell.
0256| 
0257| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0258| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0259| 
0260| ```sh
0261| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]"
0262| python -m pytest -q
0263| ```

0001| # Changelog
0002| 
0003| All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
0004| 
0005| The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
0006| and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
0007| 
0008| ## [Unreleased]
0009| 
0010| ### Added
0011| 
0012| - Open an interactive session when the client starts with no arguments — `forgel-code` now shows a prompt and stays open instead of printing usage text. A sentence typed at the prompt is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session shows the selected project and lets the owner switch it without leaving, shows a plan as its ordered tasks with their states and a new task with its title and state, and re-reads the task and release state from the engine on its own so progress appears without asking for a status. Accepting a task, sending it back with remarks, retrying a failed task, pausing and resuming work are asked for in plain language, an ambiguous or unmatched request gets a clarification and performs nothing, a failure shows the reason and the next possible step while the session stays usable, and replies follow the language of the owner's message. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit separate actions that a sentence never triggers, key material never reaches the screen, and leaving — or the end of the input — ends the session at once. The session adds no capability: every answer and every piece of state still comes from the engine, and every one-shot usage keeps its previous output, exit status and `--json` form.
0013| 
0014| ### Changed
0015| 
0016| - Speed up the suite without weakening a test — the expensive duplicated work is gone instead of a scenario: one read-only checkout copy and one prepared installation per scenario group are shared by the tests that only read them, and the bounded-check cases configure a limit below the product default.
0017| - Remove every statement of a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound from the documentation — the README `## Tests` section still says that one documented command runs the whole suite, that the installer situations are covered by a real installation into a throwaway home location with a real detected login shell, and that a run from a source checkout needs only the Python standard library and no network access, but it no longer promises how long such a run takes.
0018| 
0019| ### Fixed
0020| 
0021| - Refuse a free-text request to create or change key material, to change configuration and to create or scaffold a project in English and in Russian, including their bare wording — a sentence that names a key without any credential term, the configuration without the word `configuration`, or a project that is scaffolded rather than created is now recognised, refused in the session and never forwarded to the engine, and the refusal states that the action needs the explicit operation and names the client's own `forgel-code` command to use. Ordinary conversation that merely mentions a key, the configuration or a project still reaches the engine unchanged, and every refusal that already existed keeps its wording.
0022| - Mask the value of the French password label when it is written with underscores or hyphens — the label is now recognised as a secret label in its joined spellings as well as its spaced one, in any letter case, so an engine reply or error that carries it next to a value is redacted before display and before retention. Every value form already handled for the spaced label is covered, a joined label without an adjacent value leaves the message unchanged, and every other supported label in every language redacts exactly as before.
0023| - Refuse sensitive explicit actions phrased in French and Spanish as well as in English and Russian — a free-text request to create a project, to set or define a credential such as a password, a token or a key, or to change configuration or settings is recognised in all four languages the session speaks, in either word order, in ordinary inflections and with or without diacritics. The refusal-and-redirect answer speaks the language of the message, states that such an action is never carried out from a sentence, and then points at the client's own explicit command `forgel-code` together with the action it performs — creating a project, setting or defining a password, a token or a key, or changing the configuration — in the same style as the English and Russian refusals. Nothing of the refused request is sent onward, ordinary French and Spanish conversation still reaches the engine unchanged, and English and Russian results stay exactly as they were.
0024| - Mask the credential of a label followed by an ordinary descriptor word — a secret label followed by a word such as `value`, `field` or `string` used to hide that descriptor and leave the credential itself on screen and in the retained state; the descriptor now stays readable and the value, including the one behind a copula or a separator, is replaced by the existing masking placeholder. Sentences that only mention a secret word are still shown unchanged.
0025| - Remove the PATH block from the profile named by `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` — `--uninstall` again cleans the marked block out of the profile the override variable names, in addition to the six standard profile files, so a block left by a completed install or by an install that failed its fresh-shell check no longer survives.
0026| - Point the README install, update and uninstall commands at the current `v0.1.1` release installer — the documented commands no longer fetch the stale install script, all three name one and the same install-script URL, and the guard in `tests/test_readme_install.py` fails the suite when any of them carries an older tag or a divergent install-script URL.
